column1: # Agent sign-in (CAP-9): the browser-process strings. See docs/CREDENTIALS.md. Terminology is fixed in
# 10-sidebar.tsv; "saved password" is 저장된 비밀번호 as the browser's own password manager says it.
# The unlock prompt is shown INSIDE the operating system's re-authentication dialog, which phrases it as
# "<app> is trying to <this>" on macOS, so the English is a verb phrase in lower case.

column2: let the agent sign in with your saved passwords
column4: Reason shown in the OS re-authentication dialog when the user unlocks agent sign-in
Trace line when the agent filled a saved login; $1 is the username, $2 the site

column2: Waiting for you: unlock saved passwords to let the agent sign in to $1
column3: 확인 필요: 에이전트가 $1에 로그인하려면 저장된 비밀번호 잠금을 해제하세요
column4: Trace line when a task is paused until the user unlocks agent sign-in; $1 is the site

column2: Waiting for you: finish the verification on $1
column3: 확인 필요: $1에서 본인 확인을 마쳐 주세요
column4: Trace line when a task is paused for a one-time code, passkey or CAPTCHA the agent must not answer; $1 is the site

column2: Did not sign in to $1: your settings do not allow it
column4: Trace line when agent sign-in is refused by policy or by the per-site list; $1 is the site
Trace line when the password manager has no login for the site; $1 is the site

column2: Several saved logins for $1; asked which one to use
column3: $1에 저장된 로그인 정보가 여러 개라 어느 것을 쓸지 물었습니다
column4: Trace line when more than one account matches; $1 is the site

column2: No sign-in form on $1 to fill
column4: Trace line when the page has no fillable sign-in form; $1 is the site
Trace line when filling failed for another reason; $1 is the site
Trace line when the user resumes a task that waited for them; $1 is the site
